title: Air India Restores Non-Stop Flights to New York, Cutting Travel Time by Five Hours
excerpt: All four routes — Delhi and Mumbai to JFK and Newark — are non-stop again after the Rome refuelling stop was dropped, with journeys down from around 22 hours to approximately 17.
body:
• Air India has restored non-stop flights on all four India-New York routes — Delhi and Mumbai to JFK and Newark — ending the Rome refuelling stop.
  • Journey times fall by up to five hours: flights that took around 22 hours with the stop now take approximately 17 hours, the airline said on November 15.
  • Frequencies: Delhi-JFK and Mumbai-JFK daily; Delhi-Newark four times a week; Mumbai-Newark three times a week.
  • Pakistan's airspace remains closed to Indian carriers; the shorter routing uses Iraqi airspace, so timings can still change if airspace conditions shift — check your flight before booking.
Now operating: Non-stop services have resumed on all four Air India routes between Delhi/Mumbai and New York JFK/Newark, the airline announced on November 15, 2026. The Rome technical stop has been discontinued. Pakistan airspace remains closed to Indian carriers, and routings remain subject to airspace conditions.

Air India has restored non-stop flight operations between Delhi and Mumbai and New York, cutting journey times by up to five hours after the easing of airspace restrictions that had forced the airline to route its US services through a refuelling stop in Rome.

In a statement on Sunday, November 15, the airline said flights that previously took around 22 hours because of the Rome stop will now take approximately 17 hours. The restoration covers all four of its India-New York routes: Delhi and Mumbai to John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK) and to Newark Liberty International Airport (EWR).

Why the flights were stopping in Rome

Pakistan closed its airspace to Indian-registered and Indian-operated aircraft in April last year. Restrictions across parts of the Middle East amid the Iran-US war then further affected routings between India and North America, and Air India's New York services began operating with technical stops in Rome for refuelling. While Pakistan's airspace remains closed, the opening of Iraqi skies has shortened the route to New York, Hindustan Times reported.

"Kennedy International Airport (JFK) and to Newark Liberty International Airport (EWR)."

Routes, frequencies and aircraft

Air India currently operates one daily flight each between Delhi and Mumbai and JFK. It also operates four flights per week between Delhi and Newark and three flights per week between Mumbai and Newark.

Flights from Delhi to JFK and Newark use the airline's Airbus A350-900 aircraft, configured with 28 Business Class suites with full-flat beds, 24 Premium Economy seats and 264 Economy Class seats. Services from Mumbai are operated by Boeing 777-300ER aircraft with eight First Class suites, 40 flat-bed Business Class seats and 280 Economy Class seats.

For the large number of diaspora travellers who fly between the US East Coast and India, the change removes a stop and several hours from one of the longest journeys they make. Bookings and live schedules are on the Air India website.

Before planning your trip

  • Confirm your specific flight operates non-stop on your travel date — Newark services do not run daily.
  • Pakistan airspace remains closed to Indian carriers, so routings and timings can change if regional airspace conditions shift.
  • Check the final scheduled duration at booking; the approximately 17-hour figure is the airline's route estimate, not a guarantee for every departure.
